I've been farming these 20 mu in Quzhou for 25 years now, since I was 15. My old man taught me wheat-maize double cropping, and it's still the backbone of my farm — 16 mu of it. The other 4 mu I grow stevia. I started that three years back after Old Wang down the lane showed me the county buyer pays better than cotton, and he's right, but it's more work and I have to hire hands for the picking.

My household is five — me, my wife, my mother who's seventy and can't do heavy labor anymore, my daughter in high school who only helps weekends, and my son working at a factory in Handan. He sends money home, which helps, but I still watch every yuan. I'm not educated much — middle school — but I know my land. The extension agent comes around with his charts, and I listen, but after 25 years I trust what I've seen with my own eyes more than a booklet.

For the wheat, I planted in early October like always. I bought fresh improved seed this year — 50 yuan a mu — you can't save wheat seed more than two years or the vigor drops. The soil is decent, medium fertility. I put down 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at planting as my base. The agent says 15 kg nitrogen is enough, but I know my fields need a bit more. I'll topdress another 22 kg of urea at jointing in March when the wheat turns green. That's about 16 kg nitrogen total. I irrigate three times: once when the wheat wakes up in spring, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. Pumping costs about 40 yuan a mu each time, but without it the yield crashes. I spray herbicide once in spring, and I'll keep fungicide ready if I see rust like last year. Me and my wife do most of the work, but I hire three women from the village for a few days at harvest — it's too much for us alone. I expect about 420 kg per mu if the weather holds, same as last year.

Maize is the rush job. The wheat comes off in early June, and I've got maybe five days to get the maize in before the season slips away. I hire Zhang's mechanical planter — 50 yuan a mu, does the 16 mu in one day, worth every fen. I buy hybrid seed, about 35 yuan a mu, can't save it. Because of the time pressure, I put all the fertilizer down at planting: 35 kg compound and 20 kg urea per mu, about 15 kg nitrogen total. I don't have time for a second pass. I irrigate twice if the summer rains don't come — once at seedling stage, once at big trumpet. I spray herbicide at planting. The maize usually gives me 450 kg per mu. My son comes home to help with harvest in late September.

The stevia is on its own 4 mu plot. I transplant seedlings in late April, after the last frost. I plow deep and make the beds well. Fertilizer is lighter than the grain crops — 25 kg compound and 12 kg urea per mu, about 9 kg nitrogen. I water right after transplanting, then twice more through the summer. Aphids are the trouble, so I keep insecticide handy. The picking is the killer — I cut twice, July and September. Me and my wife do the tending, but for harvest I hire women from the village, about 10 days total at 80 yuan a day. I should get about 180 kg of dry leaves per mu, and the buyer pays 8 to 10 yuan per kg.

Total I'm spending about 11,500 yuan on inputs this year. That's a big chunk of cash, but my son sent 5,000 home and I have savings from last year. I'm not taking risks — if an input looks too expensive, I'll cut it. Better to make sure we have food on the table and cash for my daughter's school fees. I don't chase the highest yield; I chase a yield I can count on.
